system_prompt: You are assisting with a factual question about Thai law. State which provision applies and what it requires. Answer in English.
prompt: Somchai borrowed 100,000 baht from Malee with no agreed interest rate, repayable on 1 March 2026. He failed to pay on the due date. If Malee claims default interest for one year, how much is owed? Answer briefly, stating the rate and the amount.
raw_response:
Applicable provision: Thai Civil and Commercial Code, Section 224. It requires default interest on a money debt at the statutory rate (Section 7) plus 2% per year if no higher rate was agreed. The current statutory rate is 3.5% p.a. (Royal Decree Prescribing Interest Rate under the CCC (No. 2) B.E. 2566 (2023)).

Rate: 5.5% per annum.
Amount: 100,000 × 5.5% × 1 year = 5,500 baht interest; total owed = 105,500 baht.
